title: Playful shape and color budget
summary: Keep a cute interface recognizable by limiting the silhouette to a few large rounded forms and two semantic colors, so playfulness stays a system instead of scattered decoration.
when_to_use: The page should feel friendly or young, and the user asked for something cute rather than corporate.
avoid_when: The audience needs a formal or luxury tone, or the page is mostly long-form reading.

anatomy.purpose: One dominant rounded outline built from a handful of large shapes.
Two semantic colors for the subject, plus one background, reused instead of adding new hues.
A short bounce or squash on the primary action, not continuous decoration.

tokens.name: shape.radius
tokens.purpose: Large corner radius shared by cards and buttons.

tokens.name: color.subject.2
tokens.purpose: Second subject color. Do not introduce a third accent.

states.name: press
states.behavior: Slight squash, then release. One motion only.

responsive: The silhouette must still read at a small size; drop secondary decorations before shrinking the main shape.
accessibility: Do not rely on cuteness or color alone to explain an action.
Honor reduced motion by keeping the press feedback as a color or position change.
implementation_steps: Choose one rounded silhouette language and apply it to cards, buttons, and the mark.
Lock two subject colors and one background; reuse them for marks instead of adding hues.
Add a single press or hover motion on the primary action.
Write fresh components in the user stack. Do not copy character artwork or component source.
